title: Can two numbers share two or three nearest numbers at once?
description: Sanju and Mira read distance boards from a train. The video builds pairs of numbers that share the nearest ten and hundred, the nearest hundred and thousand, and all three.
teaching_notes: One idea: keep both numbers close enough to one round number for every place you need. Many pairs are right; watch for the slip that sharing one place means sharing all.

source: Let Us Think 3, same in two or three places
video_script.why: The child can build two numbers that share one nearest number, but not two or three at once.
video_script.substitution: Choose a round number that is a ten and a hundred (or a hundred and a thousand) and keep both numbers close to it.
video_script.anchor: Sanju and Mira reading distance boards from a train window
video_script.wrong_answer: they have the same nearest ten
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu thinks that sharing the nearest hundred means sharing the nearest ten. Five thousand two hundred and ten and five thousand two hundred and forty have the same nearest hundred but different nearest tens.

final_answer.value: (a) 5,201 and 5,204; (b) 6,980 and 7,020; (c) 6,998 and 7,001 (many answers are right)
final_answer.spoken: for example, five thousand two hundred and one and five thousand two hundred and four

maths_rules: open question: many pairs are right; these are reasoned samples
5,201 and 5,204: 1 and 4 from 5,200; nearest ten 5,200 and nearest hundred 5,200 for both
6,980 and 7,020: both 20 from 7,000; nearest hundred 7,000 and nearest thousand 7,000 for both
6,998 and 7,001: 2 below and 1 above 7,000; nearest ten, hundred and thousand all 7,000 for both
limits: closer than 5 jumps for tens, 50 for hundreds, 500 for thousands
slip: 5,210 and 5,240 share the nearest hundred 5,200 but their nearest tens are 5,210 and 5,240
video_script.design: Exercise, open question. Hint: keep both numbers close to one round number that suits every place. The video gives reasoned samples and says other pairs are fine.

beats.on_screen: a photo of the train compartment sits behind as a dimmed backdrop and fades at the end of the beat; a small title card From your book; a train window with Sanju and Mira and a distance board; three pairs of empty boxes headed ten and hundred, hundred and thousand, and all three

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='story'/>Sanju and Mira ride a train and read the distance boards.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Your book asks for two numbers with the same nearest ten and the same nearest hundred.
<bookmark mark='ask2'/>Then the same nearest hundred and thousand, and then all three at once.

beats.on_screen: the items hold still and the anchor gets an accent underline

marks.stop: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: two ladders side by side: the ten ladder and the hundred ladder, each with one round mark and a small close zone around it

marks.ten: the ten ladder shows a close zone around one ten
marks.hund: the hundred ladder shows a close zone around one hundred

narration: <bookmark mark='ten'/>Two numbers share a nearest ten when both are close to the same ten.
<bookmark mark='hund'/>They share a nearest hundred when both are close to the same hundred.
<bookmark mark='both'/>To share two places, they must be close enough for both. Try again with this.

beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows 5,210 and 5,240 share a nearest hundred; their nearest tens 5,210 and 5,240 are shown apart; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.chintu: Chintu's bubble appears with the two numbers
marks.first: the first number shows its nearest ten
marks.second: the second number shows its nearest ten
marks.strike: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>Five thousand two hundred and ten and five thousand two hundred and forty have the same nearest hundred. That means they have the same nearest ten.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The nearest ten of the first is five thousand two hundred and ten.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The nearest ten of the second is five thousand two hundred and forty.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>They are far apart, so sharing one place does not mean sharing another.

beats.on_screen: 5,201 and 5,204 sit close to 5,200, which is both a ten and a hundred
narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Keep the numbers close enough for every place you need.
<bookmark mark='a1'/>For the nearest ten and hundred, take five thousand two hundred and one.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>The second number is five thousand two hundred and four.
<bookmark mark='a3'/>Both are closer than five jumps to five thousand two hundred.
<bookmark mark='a4'/>That one round number is the nearest ten and the nearest hundred for both.

beats.on_screen: 6,980 and 7,020 sit close to 7,000, 20 jumps either side
narration: <bookmark mark='b1'/>For the nearest hundred and thousand, take six thousand nine hundred and eighty.
<bookmark mark='b2'/>The second number is seven thousand and twenty.
<bookmark mark='b3'/>Both are twenty jumps from seven thousand, closer than fifty.
<bookmark mark='b4'/>Seven thousand is the nearest hundred and the nearest thousand for both.

beats.on_screen: 6,998 and 7,001 sit close to 7,000, 2 jumps below and 1 jump above

marks.c1: 7,000 appears with a tiny close zone

narration: <bookmark mark='c1'/>For all three, take numbers very close to seven thousand.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>Six thousand nine hundred and ninety eight is two jumps below it.
<bookmark mark='c3'/>Seven thousand and one is one jump above it.
<bookmark mark='c4'/>Both are closer than five jumps. Seven thousand is the nearest ten, hundred and thousand for both.

beats.on_screen: a check line: find the nearest ten, hundred and thousand of both numbers and compare the places you chose

marks.check: the three nearest numbers of each number appear
marks.own: the words many pairs are right appear

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check, find the nearest ten, hundred and thousand of both numbers.
<bookmark mark='cmp'/>Compare the answers in the places you chose.
<bookmark mark='own'/>Many pairs work, so yours may differ from ours.
